Subject: Alignment: control plane identity sync and SSO/SCIM for private deployment

Hi John / ACME team,

Thanks for the sync yesterday — per our call I'm circulating a short alignment note so we can lock the two integration areas for the private control plane: SAML/SSO (IdP assertions + attribute map) and SCIM provisioning (group -> role mapping + deprovision flows).

Quick summary of what Redwood needs from ACME to finalize the design:
- SAML issuer + metadata (IdP metadata URL or XML)
- The assertion attributes you can emit (email, name, groups, title, employeeId) and any custom claim names.
- Preferred group naming convention (e.g., acme:eng:infra) so we can map to control-plane roles.
- SCIM endpoint details and OAuth client/credentials for provisioning.
- Expected operator/service accounts and their TTLs for short-lived workloads.

I've attached the questionnaire we discussed and our latest network diagram showing the VPC peering and NAT rules where the private control plane sits. For integration notes, see the linked ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4123.

Open questions for ACME we flagged on the call:
1) Do you plan to provision users or groups via SCIM, or will you run SCIM only for service accounts?
2) Can your IdP emit membership for nested groups? If yes, how do you represent them in assertions?
3) Certificate rotation window for SAML SSO — monthly or quarterly?

Milestones we propose:
- By 2027-05-06: finalized attribute map and SCIM client credentials
- 2027-05-10: smoke test in dedicated staging (canary tenant)
- 2027-05-20: production cutover (during agreed maintenance window)

Can the ACME security team confirm the preferred maintenance window (weeknight vs weekend)?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Alignment: control plane identity sync and SSO/SCIM for private deployment

Kim/Team,

Thanks — attached the filled questionnaire (see note) and our IdP metadata URL below. Short answers inline:
- IdP metadata: https://idp.acmecorp.com/metadata.xml
- We can emit: email, fullName, title, employeeNumber (employeeId), and groups under claim 'memberOf'.
- We do have nested groups; assertion flattens them into a comma-separated 'memberOf' claim.
- SCIM: we can provision both users and groups. We'll create an OAuth client scoped to SCIM.
- Cert rotation: quarterly is the default; we can support monthly for this integration with 48-hour notice.

Open items from our side: how does Redwood map group -> control-plane role when groups overlap? Example: user in acme:eng and acme:data, do they get union of roles or prioritized? Also: how do you map SCIM 'active' -> immediate revocation in runtime?

I've attached the signed questionnaire (acme-sso-scim-questionnaire-v1.pdf).

Regards,
John Dunbar
Director, Cloud Security
ACME Corp

Subject: Re: Alignment: control plane identity sync and SSO/SCIM for private deployment

Thanks John — very helpful. A few technical clarifications from the runtime side:

1) Group-to-role mapping: our default is UNION semantics (user gets union of roles from all matched groups). We also support explicit priority rules (highest-priority group wins) configured per-customer in the control plane if you prefer disjoint role assignment.

2) Overlap / precedence: if you want acme:eng to trump acme:contractor, we can add a small precedence table that we evaluate at provisioning time. We'll store the precedence mapping in the private control plane config and version it.

3) SCIM active -> runtime revocation: SCIM "active":false will trigger immediate deprovisioning in the control plane and a token revocation call for active sessions. There is a configurable grace period (default 0s for security-sensitive customers).

4) Service accounts and TTLs: for operators we recommend short-lived tokens (1h - 24h) backed by rotation of service keys. You mentioned service accounts with longer lived credentials — we suggest we gate those behind an additional approval workflow and store keys in your KMS (HSM option available for private deployments).

5) Testing/canary: we'll set up a dedicated canary customer in our staging environment that mirrors your group naming. We propose a small scripted scenario for validation: create user U in acme:eng and acme:data, verify role union, then set SCIM active:false and assert access revocation within 30s.

I'll draft the mapping example and push to the drive link; Kimberly, can you add the precedence table to the ticket?

- Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: John Dunbar <john.dunbar@acmecorp.com>

Subject: Re: Alignment: control plane identity sync and SSO/SCIM for private deployment

Marcus, Kimberly — this all sounds workable. A couple of policy/ops asks from ACME Security:

- Precedence table: we'll provide a short list of priority rules (contracts > employees > contractors) and expect Redwood to enforce that during provisioning.
- Token revocation proof: we require an audit log entry for every SCIM-triggered deprovision that contains user, timestamp, and action id. Can Redwood surface that in the control plane logs (safely redacted)?
- Maintenance windows: prefer Saturday 02:00–06:00 PT for production cutovers. Weeknight windows are tough for our ops team.

Also: attached is a short note from our infra team requesting a canary plan and a pen-test window. We prefer the pen-test no earlier than two weeks after cutover.

On the cert rotation question: quarterly rotation OK; monthly is also acceptable if we schedule a blackout during rotations.

Thanks — I'll upload the SCIM client once the internal PR is approved (ETA 48 hours).

Appreciate the quick turnaround, John. Summary and next steps:

- ACME: provide precedence table (contracts > employees > contractors) and upload SCIM OAuth client creds (John) — ETA 2027-05-06 EOD
- Redwood: enable UNION mapping by default; add optional precedence override as a config (Marcus) — ETA 2027-05-07
- Redwood: expose SCIM-triggered deprovision audit entries in control plane logs and include action id (Priyom) — ETA 2027-05-10
- Both: schedule canary smoke test in staging and confirm Saturday 02:00–06:00 PT maintenance window for production cutover. Proposed cutover weekend: 2027-05-20/21.

We'll create the canary runbook (INF-4123) and share the verification checklist in the Drive link. For the pen-test request, agreed to wait two weeks post-cutover; please share your preferred vendor and scope so we can coordinate.

If there are no blockers I'll set up a 60-minute runbook review for Friday 2027-05-07 09:00 PT. Please accept the calendar invite if that works.

Thanks all — going to close this loop in the ticket once the precedence table and SCIM creds are uploaded.

Best,
